title: Mental health strategy: initiatives, indicators and public data
asked: Ms He Ting Ru asked for an update on key initiatives under the National Mental Health and Well-Being Strategy since its 2023 launch, whether time-bound targets, baselines or KPIs have been set, and how the Government assesses whether the strategy is on track.
response: Dr Koh Poh Koon listed the initiatives rolled out since 2023: care guided by the Tiered Care Model, standardised assessments and referral pathways, expanded capacity across acute, primary, community and long-term care, the mindline 1771 first-stop service, a competency training framework that has trained over 160,000 frontline personnel and volunteers, public education efforts such as Parenting for Wellness and the Positive Use Guide, and workplace mental health support. The National Mental Health Office was set up in 2024 to coordinate these multi-agency initiatives, including setting and tracking population-level and programme-specific indicators, with performance and targets regularly reviewed. On publishing data, he said the answer is yes and that the office will look at sharing more data publicly over time, noting the strategy is just over two years old and that the office focuses on medium- to longer-term trends.

key_points.point: Mental health service providers have been guided to operate on the Tiered Care Model so clients receive care in the most appropriate setting.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we have guided our mental health service providers to operate based on the Tiered Care Model

key_points.point: A first-stop service, national mindline 1771, was set up to help people navigate and access mental health services.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we have also established the First Stop for Mental Health services such as our national mindline 1771

key_points.point: Over 160,000 frontline personnel and volunteers have been trained to identify individuals in mental distress and guide them to support.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We have also trained over 160,000 frontline personnel and volunteers

key_points.point: The Well-Being Champions Network grew from 54 founding member organisations to 800 over two years.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the Well-Being Champions Network has grown from 54 founding member organisations to 800 over the last two years

key_points.point: The National Mental Health Office was established in 2024 to coordinate and oversee multi-agency mental health initiatives.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we established the National Mental Health Office (NMHO) in 2024 to coordinate and oversee these multi-agency mental health initiatives

key_points.point: The office sets and tracks population-level and programme-specific indicators covering outcomes, access to care, literacy and attitudes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: setting and tracking population-level and programme-specific indicators

left_open: Whether time-bound targets or baselines have been established for the strategy
Whether the 2016 treatment gap figure of about 78% of individuals not seeking treatment has been re-measured
Measurable outcomes such as rates of self-harm, suicide attempts or help-seeking behaviour since 2023
A public dashboard along the lines of Australia's National Mental Health Performance Framework
supplementary: Whether mental health data and indicators will be published publicly, and what measurable outcomes and treatment-gap changes have been observed.
